lines.text: Poland just sent commandos to its border with Russia. Right next to NATO's weakest spot.
Monday. Poland launches a border operation. Police, counterterror units, GROM special forces.
Intelligence warned armed groups might cross from Kaliningrad in the first half of November.
lines.say: Intelligence warned armed groups might cross from Kah-LEE-nin-grad in the first half of November.

lines.text: Just after midnight, flashlights near the border by Sepopol. The group pulled back into Russia.
lines.say: Just after midnight, flashlights near the border by Sem-poh-pol. The group pulled back into Russia.

lines.text: Kaliningrad. A piece of Russia inside NATO. About twelve thousand troops. Iskander missiles.
lines.say: [short pause] Kah-LEE-nin-grad. A piece of Russia inside NATO. About twelve thousand troops. Iss-KAN-der missiles.

lines.text: Southeast, Belarus. Between them, sixty-five kilometers of Poland and Lithuania. The Suwalki Gap.
lines.say: Southeast, Belarus. Between them, sixty-five kilometers of Poland and Lithuania. The Soo-VAHL-kee Gap.

lines.text: It is the only land link between the Baltic states and the rest of NATO.
Close it, and three NATO countries are cut off by land.
Russia doesn't need to close it. It needs you to think it might.
Drones. Arson. Flashlights at the border. Always just under the line that triggers NATO.
Poland's operation runs until at least Sunday. After that, the gap is still there.
